headline: Nature reports that China now has far more active AI researchers than the United States and keeps more of its own AI graduates at home than before, but is still estimated to trail the US frontier by three to seven months.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a detailed Nature analysis built on named datasets and studies, but it is analysis and the gap estimate is one expert's view.
importance_line: Students and researchers choosing where to work, and governments weighing visa and chip-export policy, are affected first, then universities and AI companies in both countries, but publication counts are an imperfect measure of AI strength and the months-behind figure is one analyst's estimate.
summary: Nature News reports, drawing on data from Digital Science and a Carnegie China study, that China has about 51,000 active AI researchers against 14,000 in the United States, and that 69% of China-educated authors at the NeurIPS AI research conference now stay in China, up from 57% in 2022. Scott Singer of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, a US think tank, says China is probably three to seven months behind the US frontier, a lag Nature links to far fewer advanced chips and much less investment, while the question of whether Chinese firms catch up by distilling, meaning training on the outputs of, US models remains disputed.
